A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoMiGS research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-2 fine-tuning results, routing analyses, ablations and resource-heterogeneity experiments in Section 4 and Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds Llama 3.2 evaluations, additional baseline comparisons and router analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The main CoMiGS architecture and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix F.3 introduces an analytical linear-expert variant with auxiliary routing distributions, a KL-penalized relaxation and three alternating minimization blocks (Equation 28). This is a limited methodological extension; the PDFs do not establish its use in the language-model experiments.

E1.justification: v3 retains Multilingual Wikipedia, SlimPajama and AG News, and adds Common Corpus evaluation using YouTube-Commons, public-domain books, EU tenders and Harvard US patents. This substantially expands represented domains, particularly transcripts, procurement documents and patents. The existing languages and next-token prediction task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated pFedMoE and FDLoRA comparisons to Table 1, and FedSA-LoRA and pFedMoE to the extended appendix comparison. pFedMoE was only discussed in v1. FFA-LoRA was already evaluated in v1 Appendix C.1, while the heterogeneous-model comparison retains HetLoRA and FlexLoRA.

E3.justification: v3 adds Llama 3.2-1B alongside GPT-2-124M, with 10 communication rounds for AG News and 20 for Common Corpus (Appendix B.1). It also introduces matched-parameter resource accounting for GPT-2 with bfloat16 assumptions (Table 3). The stated GPT-2 splits, training budgets, batch size and context length are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds an AG News layer-wise routing comparison against pFedMoE (Figure 4) and fills previously unavailable AG News results for training-batch router-update ablations (Table 5). The update-frequency sweep, load-balancing ablation, expert-count/data-quantity studies and token-routing case studies largely carry over.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across three seeds for the principal and extended benchmark comparisons. No changed run-count policy, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure is documented; additional rows follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original GPT-2 CoMiGS scores are retained, but several baseline scores change: Table 1's Multilingual Local perplexity changes from 55.49 (0.64) to 54.38 (0.32). v3 adds numerous comparator and Llama results, including CoMiGS-1G1S perplexities of 18.37 (0.03) on Common Corpus and 16.31 (0.05) on AG News, plus resource-cost results in Table 3. These additions do not establish same-setting CoMiGS performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 contains the bilevel objective and load-balancing equations but no convergence theorems. v3 Section 3.4 and Appendix F add fixed-point and contraction assumptions, linear-convergence theorems and proofs, quadratic/local analyses, and a strongly convex relaxed linear-expert construction. The guarantees concern idealized optimization under additional assumptions.

C1.justification: The personalization and joint data/resource-heterogeneity claims persist. v3 adds conditional convergence guarantees, quantified resource efficiency and a released collaborative-LLM codebase as explicit contributions. The abstract and conclusion consequently claim theoretical support and practical resource efficiency beyond v1's predominantly empirical contribution.

C2.justification: v3 expands explanations of layer-dependent expert specialization and attributes negligible Llama fine-tuning gains on Wikipedia/SlimPajama to likely pretraining overlap. v1's explicit validation-data scarcity warning disappears; v3 instead emphasizes fresh training batches as an in-distribution fallback. The limitations concerning overfitting on easy tasks and vulnerability to attackers remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit project-code release statement and access link, Llama-specific training schedules, Common Corpus token counts and resource-accounting assumptions. Most existing hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain. Conversely, v1's exact GPT-2 module-name list and explicit attention-LoRA aggregation detail are omitted. The PDFs establish the new access disclosure, not the repository's actual contents.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning through on-device LLM literature and optimization foundations, including Stackelberg, Chen et al. (2021), Nesterov, and Jordan and Jacobs. It adds substantive relationships to FDLoRA and FedSA and revises the comparison with pFedMoE. Several earlier MoE references, including Wu et al. and Zadouri et al., are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten around on-device motivation and hierarchical optimization. Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix A, user-specific analysis becomes Section 4.4, and terminology, headings and appendix organization change substantially. These revisions exceed the prose needed simply to insert new results.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main layout, adds a chat illustration, redraws the method diagram and removes v1's data-split bubble figure. Tables gain model/distribution groupings and new entries; plots gain descriptive user labels. Existing learning curves and routing panels are relocated or split between the main text and appendices, alongside the new pFedMoE comparison.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens empirical support by moving beyond a single small backbone and directly comparing closely related personalized methods. Resource accounting and the project-code disclosure also make practical claims easier to assess. The new theory exposes assumptions, although it does not establish convergence of the actual federated training runs. Reporting drawbacks include unexplained pFedMoE SlimPajama values of 25.40 in Table 1 versus 22.91 in Table 5 and removal of the explicit validation-scarcity warning. These weaknesses do not outweigh the stronger empirical coverage and comparative scrutiny.
